title: Model intake declarations and semver contract for community weights
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Clarify the contract and surface area for onboarding community/open model weights into the public model catalog. This ticket defines the manifest fields, minimum compatibility assertions, pinning semantics, and the fallback/rollback expectations for host and private deployments.
background: We continue to add community models to the catalog but have inconsistent metadata and different teams interpreting pinning and compatibility differently. This has caused rollout surprises where a model variant with a different KV cache layout or tokenization produced errors in hosted and dedicated runtimes. We need a single agreed contract and acceptance criteria to reduce support load and prevent runtime incidents.
goals: Define a minimal model manifest schema (human-readable) that must be supplied on intake
Specify explicit compatibility flags and a recommended set of machine-verifiable checks
Establish version pinning semantics and graceful fallback rules for incompatible variants
Provide acceptance criteria and test cases for onboarding engineers to validate new entries
Align Console UI fields and API validation errors with the contract
out_of_scope: Automated full-compatibility verification across all HW targets (covered by infra workstream)
Model performance benchmarking; only compatibility/structural metadata required
Full migration tooling for older catalog entries (separate cleanup EPIC)
requirements: Manifest v1 fields required: id, display_name, source_url, weights_url, framework, framework_version, tokenizer, max_sequence_length, kv_cache_layout, quantization_profiles, recommended_variant
Compatibility flags required (boolean or enumerated): kv_cache_compatible_with, tokenizer_compatibility, supports_prefix_cache, supports_streaming, supports_batched_inference
Semantic versioning: model versions must follow semver-like pattern X.Y.Z and include a 'variant' label for quantized or optimized builds

Pinning API: catalog API must accept 'pin_version' and 'pin_mode' where pin_mode is one of [strict, tolerant, rolling]; strict prevents fallback, tolerant allows nearest compatible variant, rolling uses alias that moves with new validated releases

Fallback rules: when a pinned variant is unavailable or incompatible, tolerant must select a pre-declared fallback list in the manifest; if none, the call returns 409 Conflict with suggested compatible variants
Validation: server-side manifest validation returns structured errors with field path and remediation guidance; Console shows the same error text
Private/VPC deployments: manifest must include 'private_compat_notes' that operators can use for air-gapped QA steps
Telemetry: onboarding flow must create a catalog ingestion event and tag entries with 'compatibility_status' (unknown | verified | flagged)
Docs: PRD must include example manifests for a huggingface-style weights bundle, an optimized quantized variant, and a multi-file tokenizer setup
acceptance_criteria: A canonical manifest template exists in the repo and is reviewed by infra and runtime teams
API schema validation implemented and returns deterministic error messages for at least the required fields
Compatibility flags are surfaced in the Console model detail page and editable during intake
Pinning modes behave per spec in unit tests: strict blocks implicit fallbacks; tolerant resolves to first compatible fallback; rolling updates alias pointers in the catalog API
Automated smoke test: ingest three sample community models (vanilla, quantized, tokenizer-split) and verify runtime can load the recommended_variant on hosted and a simulated dedicated config
Acceptance docs contain step-by-step onboarding checklist and a 'known failure' troubleshooting appendix
Security review sign-off recorded as a checklist item and KMS/HSM notes added when weights_url implies private storage
rollout_plan: Phase 1: publish manifest template and API validation (catalog-2.3). Phase 2: Console UI changes to show compatibility flags and pin controls. Phase 3: pilot with 3 community models and remediate issues. Phase 4: general availability and deprecation notice for legacy ad-hoc entries.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Teams may publish manifests missing implicit tokenizer files. Mitigation: validation detects tokenizer pattern mismatches and blocks ingestion with remediation steps.

Risk: Pinning strict could cause customer outages if underlying hardware lacks a required kernel. Mitigation: require a verification step and 'verified_on' list of HW families in manifest before allowing strict pinning for hosted tiers.
Risk: Operators for Private deployments may need per-customer QA. Mitigation: include 'private_compat_notes' field and a checklist template for on-prem engineers.
notes: Discussed with runtime team on 2025-08-20: KV cache layout differences are the top source of incompatibility; we should include a machine-readable layout hash in manifest
Design requested UI copy for pin modes; we will iterate in a follow-up DES ticket
PM will coordinate with Solutions Engineering for pilot customers and prepare a readiness doc
